lessons.title: NumPy Fundamentals
lessons.html:
NumPy - Numerical Computing

NumPy is the foundation of data science in Python. Handles arrays and mathematical operations efficiently.

Creating Arrays:

import numpy as np

# From list
arr = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])

# Zeros and ones
zeros = np.zeros(10)
ones = np.ones((3, 3))

# Range
range_arr = np.arange(0, 10, 2)  # [0,2,4,6,8]

print(arr.shape, arr.dtype)

Vectorized Operations:

a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
b = np.array([4, 5, 6])

sum_ab = a + b      # [5,7,9]
product = a * b     # [4,10,18]
mean = np.mean(a)   # 2.0

lessons.title: Pandas DataFrames
lessons.html:
Pandas - Data Manipulation

Pandas provides DataFrames - Excel-like tables for Python.

Creating DataFrames:

import pandas as pd

# From dictionary
data = {
    'name': ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie'],
    'age': [25, 30, 35],
    'city': ['NY', 'LA', 'Chicago']
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# From CSV
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

Basic Operations:

# Select columns
names = df['name']

# Filter rows
young = df[df['age'] < 30]

# Add column
df['adult'] = df['age'] >= 18

# Group by
avg_age = df.groupby('city')['age'].mean()

lessons.title: Data Visualization
lessons.html:
Matplotlib & Seaborn

Create publication-quality charts for data analysis.

Matplotlib Basics:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
y = np.sin(x)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(x, y, label='sin(x)')
plt.title('Sine Wave')
plt.xlabel('x')
plt.ylabel('sin(x)')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

Seaborn (Higher level):

import seaborn as sns

sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='age', y='salary', hue='city')
plt.title('Salary vs Age by City')
plt.show()

lessons.title: Data Cleaning
lessons.html:
Handling Missing & Dirty Data

Real data is messy. Learn to clean it properly.

Detecting Issues:

# Missing values
print(df.isnull().sum())

# Duplicates
print(df.duplicated().sum())

# Data types
print(df.dtypes)

Cleaning Operations:

# Fill missing
df['salary'].fillna(df['salary'].mean(), inplace=True)

# Drop missing
df.dropna(subset=['email'], inplace=True)

# Remove duplicates
df.drop_duplicates(inplace=True)

# Fix data types
df['age'] = pd.to_numeric(df['age'], errors='coerce')

lessons.title: Statistical Analysis
lessons.html:
Descriptive Statistics

Summarize and understand your data.

Basic Stats:

# Single column
print(df['salary'].describe())

# All numeric columns
print(df.describe())

# Correlation matrix
print(df.corr())

Custom Analysis:

# Group statistics
grouped = df.groupby('department')['salary'].agg([
    'count', 'mean', 'std', 'min', 'max'
])

# Cross-tabulation
pivot = pd.pivot_table(df, values='salary', index='department', columns='gender')

lessons.title: Machine Learning Intro
lessons.html:
Scikit-learn Basics

Build your first ML model in 10 lines!

Linear Regression:

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error

X = df[[ 'experience', 'education' ]]
y = df['salary']

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)

model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test, y_pred))
print(f'RMSE: {rmse:.2f}')

lessons.title: End-to
lessons.html:
Complete Data Science Workflow

From raw data → cleaned → visualized → modeled.

Pipeline Example:

from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
    ('model', LinearRegression())
])

pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred = pipeline.predict(X_test)

Project Steps:

  1. Load & explore data
  2. Clean missing values
  3. Feature engineering
  4. Train/test split
  5. Model training & evaluation
  6. Visualize results
  7. Save model
